query: What signals suggest an agent's tickets will take longer to resolve?

per_column.name: issue_domain
per_column.rationale: Categorizes the ticket by technical domain from short_description; a genuine axis to compare resolution time across issue types. Values are sound readings of the source text (e.g. 'Unable to access the database' -> database_access).

per_column.name: infrastructure_scope
per_column.rationale: Whether the issue affects shared vs single-user infrastructure is a plausible driver of resolution time. However the short descriptions rarely state scope explicitly; labeling 'Unable to access the database' as shared_service or a VPN issue as shared_service is an inference that is reasonable but sometimes goes beyond what the text supports.

per_column.name: technical_severity_signal
per_column.rationale: Distinguishing access_failure vs degraded_performance vs outage is a useful severity axis for resolution time. Mostly a warranted reading (e.g. 'frequent disconnection' -> degraded_performance, 'Unable to access' -> access_failure), though borderline for terse descriptions.

per_column.name: assigned_agent
per_column.rationale: Directly relevant since the query asks about per-agent resolution time; provides the grouping key. Appears to be a normalized copy of the original assigned_to field, so well grounded. Slightly redundant with an existing column but still central to the query.

per_column.name: resolution_complexity_indicator
per_column.rationale: Complexity (single_action_fix vs multi_step_troubleshooting vs vendor_escalation) is highly relevant to how long tickets take. But these labels are inferred confidently from very terse descriptions that do not state remediation effort; the specific complexity assignment is often not supported by the source text.

per_column.name: agent_handoff_pattern
per_column.rationale: Whether a ticket was closed by a different person than assigned, or was unassigned, is a strong signal for longer resolution. Derivable from original assigned_to/closed_by fields, so well grounded.

judge.rationale: All six columns give genuine, non-trivial axes for analyzing what drives longer resolution times (domain, severity, complexity, scope, agent identity, and handoff behavior); none are near-constant or bare-sentiment restatements. Groundedness is mixed: agent, handoff, and issue_domain are well supported by source fields/text, while infrastructure_scope and resolution_complexity_indicator assert fairly specific characterizations that the terse short_descriptions do not clearly warrant, introducing some inference risk.
